title: IFNA: catch only a missing match

screens.prompt: In B9, look the code in A8 up in the table and say not on the list when it is missing.

hints.syntax: =IFNA(VLOOKUP(A8,A2:B7,2,FALSE),"not on the list"): the fallback is the second argument.
hints.func-ifna: Only #N/A is replaced here. A broken reference would stay on screen for someone to fix.
hints.func-vlookup: The price sits in the second column of A2:B7.
hints.require-ref: Read the code from A8 instead of typing Q-9 into the formula.
hints.value: Q-9 is not in the code column, so the fallback words are the answer.
hints.error: The grader rejects a TRUE fourth argument: it answers 32 for Q-9 and the fallback never runs.

reject.why: an approximate lookup answers 32 from the last row instead of reporting a miss
IFERROR also hides #REF! and #VALUE!, which this question does not want
the code is typed into the formula instead of read from the grid
an index and match finds the row, but this lesson asks for the lookup function itself
there is no third column, and IFNA does not catch #REF!
the text fallback is then divided by zero
the missing comma leaves one argument where two are expected

screens.prompt: In B9, price the code in A2 with the same lookup, keeping the fallback for a missing code.

hints.syntax: The same call with A2 in place of A8: =IFNA(VLOOKUP(A2,A2:B7,2,FALSE),"not on the list").
hints.func-ifna: Keep the guard even though this row is found. The formula is meant for the rows that miss.
hints.func-vlookup: Column 2 of the table holds the price.
hints.require-ref: Take the code from A2 rather than typing A-1.
hints.value: A-1 first appears in row 2 at 10. The duplicate at row 5 holds 12 and is never reached.
hints.error: IFNA lets a #DIV/0! through, so dividing this price by zero shows the error rather than the price.

reject.why: the lookup is unguarded, so a code that is not on the list would show an error
the first column returns the code A-1 instead of the price
a different range is searched, so the code in the grid is never read
an index and match finds the row, but this lesson asks for the lookup function itself
the table has two columns, so the column number is out of range and #REF! escapes IFNA
the found price is then divided by zero
the missing comma inside VLOOKUP breaks the argument list

docs.explain:
IFNA evaluates its first argument and returns the second only when that argument fails with #N/A. A lookup that finds nothing raises exactly that error, which makes IFNA the narrow net around a missing code. Every other error passes through untouched.

Here Q-9 sits in A8, and the code column runs A-1, B-2, C-3, then the same three again. A lookup that demands an exact match finds nothing and prints not on the list. The second screen asks about A-1, which is in A2 at 10.

An approximate match returns 32 for Q-9 and never reaches the fallback, because a near miss counts as a match. Set the fourth argument to FALSE. Keep the guard on the second screen too, where the code is found, because the same formula gets copied to rows that miss.

errors.text: The lookup matched nothing; without the guard this is the error B9 would hold.
The function name is typed as IFNAA or IFA, and Excel reads what is there without guessing.
The fourth argument is set to TRUE or left out, so an approximate match answers 32 for Q-9 and the fallback never fires.

docs.atWork: Pricing an order line from a product list, where a code nobody stocks should say so instead of showing #N/A.
docs.outcome: Replace a missing lookup match and leave every other error visible.
docs.teaches: IFNA around VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP and INDEX/MATCH, and which errors it leaves alone
docs.dataset: Code and price table with one code the table does not hold

seo.title: IFNA in Excel: catch only a missing match
seo.description: IFNA replaces #N/A and leaves every other error in place, so a broken range still shouts. IFERROR hides both behind the same friendly word.
